name: Brute Force
desc: Commonly found in login systems; large-scale attempts of login credentials against a known username.

name: SMS Bombing
desc: Replaying the SMS verification-code request to flood a target with text messages (SMS bombing).

name: Authentication Bypass
desc: The application lacks a valid token mechanism, allowing authentication information to be modified to bypass server-side authorization.

name: Malicious Registration
desc: The user registration function can be abused by an attacker to perform bulk registration.

name: Session Fixation
desc: The session ID does not change before and after login, creating a session-hijacking risk.

name: Plaintext Password Transmission
desc: Usernames or passwords are transmitted without encryption, making them susceptible to sniffing and interception.

name: Password Recovery Logic Flaw
desc: Logic flaws in the password recovery flow can be exploited to illegitimately reset a password.

name: OAuth Authentication Flaw
desc: Incomplete OAuth authentication allows unauthorized login to other users' accounts.

name: Weak Password
desc: Discovery of weak passwords in the system through brute forcing, guessing, and similar techniques.

name: Broken Authentication & Session Management
desc: Vulnerabilities in the authentication and session management functions, including missing session timeout settings.

name: CAPTCHA Functional Flaw
desc: The CAPTCHA does not expire and can be reused, enabling brute-force attacks.

name: Username Enumeration
desc: Different accounts return different error messages, allowing enumeration of valid accounts in the system.

name: CORS Cross-Origin Resource Sharing Vulnerability
desc: Improper CORS configuration can be exploited to steal users' sensitive data.

name: Flash Cross-Domain Access Vulnerability
desc: An incorrect crossdomain.xml policy leads to cross-domain security issues.

name: Outdated jQuery Version
desc: An outdated jQuery version introduces cross-site scripting and other known security vulnerabilities.

name: JSONP Hijacking
desc: Cross-domain data transfer lacks authorization checks, allowing sensitive data to be read by malicious scripts.

name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
desc: Forces an authenticated user to perform unintended actions within a web application.

name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
desc: Injects malicious scripts into web pages, executing malicious code when the page is viewed.

name: Code Injection
desc: An attacker submits code as input, which the server processes as dynamic code.

name: LDAP Injection
desc: Leverages LDAP query syntax to disclose sensitive user and host information.

name: Command Injection
desc: Injects OS commands via an HTTP request to execute system commands on the server.

name: XFF Injection
desc: Performs SQL injection by manipulating the X-Forwarded-For header.

name: SSI Injection
desc: May allow injection of code into HTML pages and even remote code execution.

name: SQL Injection
desc: By inserting SQL queries, an attacker can read or tamper with data, perform administrative operations, or execute system commands.

name: XPath Injection
desc: Injects elements into an XPath query, potentially bypassing authentication.

name: Link or Frame Injection
desc: Injects frame or iframe tags containing malicious content.

name: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
desc: XML external entities can be abused to read system files, perform SSRF, and mount other attacks.

name: Local File Inclusion
desc: Includes and executes code on the target server to obtain sensitive files or privileges.

name: Vertical Privilege Escalation
desc: A low-privilege account can access or operate high-privilege functionality.

name: Unauthorized Access
desc: Internal resources or functions can be accessed directly without login or authorization.

name: Arbitrary File Upload
desc: Uploading an executable script file to gain the ability to run commands on the server.

name: Arbitrary File Download
desc: System files, configuration files, and similar can be browsed or downloaded arbitrarily.

name: Horizontal Privilege Escalation
desc: Users at the same privilege level can access or operate other users' resources.

name: Remote File Inclusion
desc: Crafting parameters to include remote code that is executed on the server.

name: Error Page Information Disclosure
desc: Error messages contain sensitive server or database information.

name: Test / Backup File Leak
desc: Leftover outdated files, backup pages, and test files are exposed.

name: .git Source Code Leak
desc: The .git directory was not removed at deployment, allowing source code to be recovered.

name: GitHub Information Leak
desc: Sensitive code, keys, and similar are inadvertently made public on GitHub.

name: IIS Short Filename Disclosure
desc: An IIS file enumeration vulnerability that allows enumeration of files in the root directory.

name: Absolute Path Disclosure
desc: The application discloses its absolute path on the host.

name: Directory Listing
desc: A website configuration flaw results in a browsable directory listing vulnerability.

name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
desc: Configuration files contain sensitive data such as passwords, keys, internal addresses, and employee identifiers.

name: Sensitive File Leak
desc: Program files, configuration files, logs, backups, and database files are exposed.

name: Default Page Leak
desc: Default-installed middleware and frameworks ship with sample pages and documentation.

name: Directory Traversal
desc: An attacker views the website's directory structure and files to mount further attacks.

name: Residual Intrusion Traces
desc: Traces of a prior intrusion remain in the application, such as WebShell files.

name: SVN Source Code Leak
desc: Source code is obtained through an SVN source code disclosure vulnerability.

name: Web Console Exposure
desc: The management console of a web container or database is exposed.

name: Insecure HTTP Methods
desc: The server enables insecure methods such as TRACE, PUT, and DELETE.

name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
desc: The server makes requests on the attacker's behalf, allowing access to internal-network or local resources.

name: Host Header Attack
desc: Malicious manipulation of the HTTP Host header to enable phishing, cache poisoning, and similar attacks.

name: Slow HTTP DoS Attack
desc: Exhausts server resources through slow HTTP requests.

name: Unnecessary Web Server Ports Open
desc: Default ports beyond the required business ports are left open.

name: Insecure Storage
desc: Important information is not encrypted or is encrypted with insufficient strength.

name: Sensitive Information in HTML
desc: HTML pages contain sensitive information.
